Hi all — I reviewed the sim and the QPS numbers. Quick technical notes:

- Feasibility: 2,800 QPS with 14–24 token responses is achievable on a 12-GPU dedicated pool with model quantization and request batching tuned for small outputs. We would recommend an instance mix with lower-latency GPUs and explicit KV cache warm-up.

- Preemption/queueing behavior: our current reserved pool scheduler supports three priority bands: Critical (no preemption, highest weight), Standard (preemption allowed under extreme contention), and Background (preemptable). For Reserved (paid) pools we can map your critical route to the Critical band for business hours. Outside of business hours the Critical band remains but headroom is reduced.

- Suggested operational policy for your case:
  * Business hours (08:00–20:00 PT): guarantee p99 < 150ms for Critical band up to committed throughput + 25% headroom. If utilization exceeds committed + 25% for more than 10 minutes, the system will activate burst credits.
  * Burst credits: Satellite gets 6 burst credit tokens per day; each token equals 10 minutes of sustained 1.5x concurrency over the headroom baseline. Credits are pooled and expire daily.
  * Preemption window: when the cluster is under systemic pressure (e.g., data-center level maintenance or cross-tenant failover), Standard band may be throttled with 30-second graceful drain and retry semantics. Critical band is evicted only under declared force-majors with 2-minute degradation notice when possible.

- Observability hooks: we can surface token-level latency and a dedicated dashboard; we recommend configuring a p99 alert tied to automatic burst credit consumption.

I will run a quick capacity validation and share a targeted top-line clause. Lauren — happy to feed technical language for the SLA.

Ben Carter
Senior Capacity Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emma — looping back with two candidate SLA clauses (summaries below). I attached a draft that contains both options and wording for credits/measurement windows.

Option A — Headroom + Burst Credits (recommended by Ops):
- During business hours (08:00–20:00 PT) Redwood guarantees p99 latency < 150ms for the Critical route up to committed throughput + 25% headroom.
- Satellite receives 6 daily burst credits; each credit grants 10 minutes of 1.5x sustained concurrency above headroom. Burst credit consumption is reported in daily usage logs.
- Failure to meet p99 targets (after accounting for burst credits) entitles Satellite to latency credits applied to next billing cycle.

Option B — Hard Throughput SLO (tighter commercial commitment):
- Redwood guarantees p99 latency < 150ms for the Critical route up to committed throughput + 10% safety margin.
- If Redwood fails to meet the SLO across any 24-hour rolling window, Satellite receives service credits proportional to impacted time.
- Requires a minimum 12-month reserved commitment and additional capacity-weighted premium.

Please review the attached SLA_Draft_Satellite_V2.pdf for full text. If you prefer Option B we’ll need an internal approval for price uplift and a signed amendment to the Reserved Capacity agreement.

Next steps: confirm preferred option, and Ben will finalize the technical runbook for 95/99 pctl behaviors and preemption flows. If needed, we can add Jordan from EdgeCloud (cc’d) to scope HW topology choices.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
